lines:
Implemented the connect-once flow and removed the stale gate that made the feature unreachable.

NATIVE
- Removed validate_unavailable_executor_enablement_update (settings_v2.rs) and its call/import (service.rs), so an external-agent target can actually be enabled. It is now gated by the readiness check instead of a build-wide "unavailable" claim.
- Added Claude Code readiness: probe_external_agent now routes claude_code to probe_claude_code, which resolves the CLI, validates STDIO args/cwd, and returns an honest "found; sign-in is verified by Claude Code on the first delegation" result. The Codex App Server handshake is unchanged.

UI
- External agents is now product-first: "Add Codex" and "Add Claude Code" create a target with all defaults pre-filled, so the user types no command, path, model or credential.
- Each card has Ready / Not ready / Not connected status, a "Check & connect" button that runs the readiness check and sets enabled=true only on success (a failure leaves it disconnected and shows the reason), and one plain permission question ("may it make changes without asking you?") mapped to the adapter's own modes.
- Technical fields (adapter, exact permission mode, model, effort, connection, credential bindings, MCP metadata, capability evidence) moved under a collapsed Advanced section. The dead "Workflow execution not available" switch and copy are gone.
- The delegation tool keeps its two DSH-style entries; its duplicate "External agent target" dropdown is replaced by a readiness line ("Connected: X." / "Not connected yet. Connect Codex under External agents."). Model/thinking still live on the External Agent node.

VERIFICATION
- cargo test -p aworkit-desktop --lib: 515 passed, 0 failed (HOME set; the job shell has no HOME).
- New a_connected_external_agent_runs_from_saved_settings_and_returns_only_its_answer drives real Settings -> resolve_delegation_target -> freeze -> product fixture process and asserts only the final answer returns. This closes the gap where the existing executor tests hand-injected the target.
- New generic_settings_may_enable_an_external_agent_target and a_claude_code_draft_reports_readiness_without_a_handshake; tests/external_agent_probe.rs green.
- Frontend: tsc --noEmit clean; vitest src/workbench: 289 passed across 31 files.
- Updated qa/desktop-browser-visual.sh for the new labels.

DEFERRED (honest gaps)
- The External Agent node selector still allows choosing a not-connected product; it annotates nothing yet and the native freeze fails safely with "no enabled <adapter> external agent is configured". Full selector gating is not done.
- Claude readiness proves the CLI resolves, not that it is signed in.
- Connection Advanced still exposes model/effort/permission-mode as optional defaults instead of removing them entirely; the workflow node remains the authoritative place.
- Browser/packaged-native QA was not executed here.

Goal
Make running Codex and Claude Code as external agents the minimum-possible setup: connect each app once, then use it in two equally supported ways. Remove every field a user cannot reasonably answer. Model and thinking effort belong in the workflow (on the node, or next to the tool), never in the connection.

Outcome for the user
Settings shows two cards, Codex and Claude Code, each with a "Check & connect" button. After the check the card is either Ready or Not ready with one plain sentence saying what to fix. There is one permission question per app. Nothing else is required. Advanced options exist but are closed by default.

THE TWO USE PATHS (both kept, same connection behind both)
1. Tool path (DeepSeek-Harness style). The model decides mid-task to delegate to a connected external agent by calling tool.subagent_codex or tool.subagent_claude_code from within an Agent step or chat. This is the original DSH use case and must keep working.
2. Workflow node path. The author places an explicit External Agent node and chooses the connected Codex or Claude Code target. Deterministic, visible in the graph.
Both paths resolve to the same one-time connection. Connecting must never need to be repeated per node or per tool.

SETTINGS: EXTERNAL AGENTS (rewritten)
- Present two product cards: Codex and Claude Code. Internally these remain the codex_app_server and claude_code adapters; keeping the adapter abstraction is fine, but the primary UI is the two named products, not a generic "target" list with an adapter dropdown.
- Each card has "Check & connect". The check may run as a non-interactive readiness check (find the executable; confirm it can start and is signed in) and then report:
  * Ready - e.g. "Codex found and signed in." Also "Claude Code found and signed in."
  * Not found - e.g. "Codex CLI not found. Install it, then check again."
  * Found but not signed in - e.g. "Codex found, but not signed in. Run `codex login`, then check again."
- The readiness result is what gates use: a Ready product is selectable in tools and nodes; a not-ready product is shown greyed out with "not set up yet" and its reason.
- One permission question per connected app, plain words, safe default:
  "While <Codex> works on a delegated task, may it make changes without asking you?"
  [Yes, let it work] (default for coding tasks) / [No, read-only - look and report only]
  This must map to the adapter's own non-interactive permission vocabulary; unsupported combinations must be refused at connect time, not at run time.
- Advanced (collapsed, empty by default): a different executable or version/location, a second account/profile (e.g. work vs personal), extra environment variables or an API key for users who do not want the app's own login.
- No model, no reasoning/thinking, no arguments, no working directory in the normal connection UI.

SETTINGS: TOOLS (keep the tools, remove their separate setup)
- Keep tool.subagent_codex ("Codex agent delegation") and tool.subagent_claude_code ("Claude Code agent delegation") in the Tools list. This is the DSH-style path and must not be removed.
- Change each tools row to: an on/off switch, a readiness line that reflects the connected product (e.g. "Codex - ready"), and, optionally, a "Not set up yet - go to External agents" link when not ready.
- Remove the tool's own "External agent target" dropdown and any per-tool target configuration. If Codex is connected, the tool uses it.
- Optional, only if it stays simple: two small optional fields next to the tool, Model and Thinking, meaning "when this assistant delegates, use these". Leave empty to use the app's own default. Do not make them required and do not duplicate them into the connection.
- Remove the dead enable switch and the "Workflow execution not available" / "Disable non-executable legacy flag" copy. Ready means usable; not ready explains why.

WORKFLOW NODE (keep, unchanged in spirit)
- Keep the External Agent node and its Model and Thinking fields. These remain the place where per-job model/thinking is set.
- The provider selector lists only connected (Ready) products; others show "not set up yet".
- Runtime precedence: an explicit node or per-call model/thinking wins; otherwise the app's own default. The connection stores no model.

RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR (must remain true after the redesign)
- The app's own login is authoritative; no passwords are entered into Aworkit by default.
- A delegation is unattended: it never stops to ask the user for approval mid-task, and its fixed permission policy is stated honestly.
- The exact resolved setup is frozen for the chat/run at first use, so later Settings changes cannot alter an already-running chat.
- Only the external agent's final answer returns to the chat; its reasoning, tool traffic, diffs and internal session never leak in. (Keep the existing normalized child frame and lineage.)

WHAT TO REMOVE
- The free-form target record: command, arguments, working directory, credential bindings, permission-mode picker, model, reasoning effort, MCP forwarding metadata.
- The duplicate second setup path for the same product.
- The "external-agent execution is unavailable" gating and copy, which is stale: the executor (Codex and Claude Code one-shot adapters) already exists and is tested. Enablement must become real and driven by the readiness check.
- Any surface that silently fails a delegation because no enabled target exists; replace with an up-front, plain-language readiness state.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A new user can go from nothing to a usable Codex delegation in External agents with exactly one button click plus one permission answer, entering no command, path, model or credential.
2. Codex and Claude Code each show a correct Ready or Not ready state, with actionable text, and re-check on demand.
3. Both use paths work from the same single connection: (a) the model calls the delegation tool inside an Agent step/chat, and (b) an explicit External Agent node runs.
4. Model and Thinking are settable on the workflow node and, if kept, optionally next to the tool; neither is required in the connection and neither is stored there.
5. The Tools rows show readiness and an on/off switch, with no second configuration screen.
6. A not-ready product cannot be selected for use and explains why; a ready product can.
7. Removing the connection/readiness gate does not silently break an already-running chat (frozen per run).
8. End-to-end test that starts from a real saved Settings document with one connected product, freezes the delegation tool, and asserts the product process ran and only its final answer returned. (Existing executor tests hand-inject the resolved target, so they do not cover the connect-to-run path; a real path test is required.)

CURRENT ANCHORS (for orientation, not a prescription)
- UI: desktop/src/workbench/settings-v2/IntegrationSections.tsx (ExternalAgentsSection), CredentialsToolsSection.tsx, ToolConfigurationEditor.tsx (DELEGATION_ADAPTERS), settings.ts / settingsDraft.ts.
- Tool manifests: desktop/tool-plugins/aworkit-native/tool-plugin.json (tool.subagent_codex, tool.subagent_claude_code; field kind external_agent_target).
- Native: desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/external_agent.rs (probe_external_agent currently Codex-only; resolve_delegation_target; build_delegation_backend), service.rs freeze_builtin_tool (resolves the target), tool_loop.rs freeze_external_agent, tool_loop/subagent/external.rs (executor), settings_v2.rs validate_unavailable_executor_enablement_update (stale enable block), graph_pass.rs run_external_agent_node.

OUT OF SCOPE / NOTES
- A generic ACP target and remote A2A agents are future work; do not build them here, but do not delete the adapter abstraction that would allow them.
- Multiple targets of the same product are only needed for the Advanced case (second account/location); a single connection per product is the default.
- Existing legacy enabled records must keep loading losslessly; migration should not lose user data.

data.title: Connect Codex and Claude Code once, then use them as a delegation tool and an External Agent node
